settings.title: PostProcessSettings
settings.description: Post process settings to use for this volume.

bOverride_TemperatureType.description: first all bOverride_... as they get grouped together into bitfields

bMobileHQGaussian.description: Enable HQ Gaussian on high end mobile platforms. (ES3_1)

bloomMethod.title: EBloomMethod
bloomMethod.description: Preferred bloom algorithm. A different method may be used if the preferred method is not available on the target platform, e.g. due to performance limits.

temperatureType.title: ETemperatureMethod
temperatureType.description:
Selects the type of temperature calculation.
White Balance uses the Temperature value to control the virtual camera's White Balance. This is the default selection.
Color Temperature uses the Temperature value to adjust the color temperature of the scene, which is the inverse of the White Balance operation.

whiteTemp.description: Controls the color temperature or white balance in degrees Kelvin which the scene considers as white light.

whiteTint.description: Controls the color of the scene along the magenta - green axis (orthogonal to the color temperature).  This feature is equivalent to color tint in digital cameras.

colorSaturation.title: Vector4
colorSaturation.description: Control the intensity of the color(hue) for the entire image.Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

colorContrast.title: Vector4
colorContrast.description: Control the range of light and dark values in your scene. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

colorGamma.title: Vector4
colorGamma.description: Control the luminance curve of the scene. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the entire image.

colorGain.title: Vector4
colorGain.description: This value multiplies the colors of the image.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the entire scene.

colorOffset.title: Vector4
colorOffset.description: This value is added to the colors of the scene.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the image being more or less washed-out.

colorSaturationShadows.title: Vector4
colorSaturationShadows.description: Control the intensity of the colors (hue) in the shadow region of the image.  Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

colorContrastShadows.title: Vector4
colorContrastShadows.description: Control the range of light and dark values in your scene. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

colorGammaShadows.title: Vector4
colorGammaShadows.description: Control the luminance curve of the shadow region. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the shadow region.

colorGainShadows.title: Vector4
colorGainShadows.description: This value multiplies the colors in the shadow region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

colorOffsetShadows.title: Vector4
colorOffsetShadows.description: This value is added to the colors in the shadow region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the shadows being more or less washed-out.

colorSaturationMidtones.title: Vector4
colorSaturationMidtones.description: Control the intensity of the colors (hue) in the mid-tone region of the image.  Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

colorContrastMidtones.title: Vector4
colorContrastMidtones.description: Control the range of light and dark values in the mid-tone region. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

colorGammaMidtones.title: Vector4
colorGammaMidtones.description: Control the luminance curve of the mid-tone region of the image. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the image.

colorGainMidtones.title: Vector4
colorGainMidtones.description: This value multiplies the colors in the mid-tone region of the image.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

colorOffsetMidtones.title: Vector4
colorOffsetMidtones.description: This value is added to the colors in the mid-tone region of the image.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the mid-tones being more or less washed-out.

colorSaturationHighlights.title: Vector4
colorSaturationHighlights.description: Control the intensity of the color (hue) for the highlights region of the image.  Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

colorContrastHighlights.title: Vector4
colorContrastHighlights.description: Control the range of light and dark values in the highlights region. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

colorGammaHighlights.title: Vector4
colorGammaHighlights.description: Control the luminance curve of the highlight region. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the highlight region.

colorGainHighlights.title: Vector4
colorGainHighlights.description: This value multiplies the colors in the highlight region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

colorOffsetHighlights.title: Vector4
colorOffsetHighlights.description: This value is added to the colors in the highlight region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the highlights being more or less washed-out.

colorCorrectionHighlightsMin.description: This value sets the lower threshold for what is considered to be the highlight region of the image.

colorCorrectionHighlightsMax.description: This value sets the upper threshold for what is considered to be the highlight region of the image.  This value should be larger than HighlightsMin. Default is 1.0, for backwards compatibility

colorCorrectionShadowsMax.description: This value sets the threshold for what is considered to be the shadow region of the image.

blueCorrection.description: Correct for artifacts with "electric" blues due to the ACEScg color space. Bright blue desaturates instead of going to violet.

expandGamut.description: Expand bright saturated colors outside the sRGB gamut to fake wide gamut rendering.

toneCurveAmount.description: Allow effect of Tone Curve to be reduced (Set ToneCurveAmount and ExpandGamut to 0.0 to fully disable tone curve)

filmSlope.description: Controls the overall steepness of the tonemapper curve.  Larger values increase scene contrast and smaller values reduce contrast.

filmToe.description: Controls the contrast of the dark end of the tonemapper curve. Larger values increase contrast and smaller values decrease contrast.

filmShoulder.description: Sometimes referred to as highlight rolloff.  Controls the contrast of the bright end of the tonemapper curve. Larger values increase contrast and smaller values decrease contrast.

filmBlackClip.description: Lowers the toe of the tonemapper curve by this amount. Increasing this value causes more of the scene to clip to black.  For most purposes, this property should remain 0

filmWhiteClip.description: Controls the height of the tonemapper curve.  Raising this value can cause bright values to more quickly approach fully-saturated white.

sceneFringeIntensity.description: in percent, Scene chromatic aberration / color fringe (camera imperfection) to simulate an artifact that happens in real-world lens, mostly visible in the image corners.

chromaticAberrationStartOffset.description: A normalized distance to the center of the framebuffer where the effect takes place.

bloomIntensity.description: Multiplier for all bloom contributions >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

bloomGaussianIntensity.description: Multiplier for Gaussian bloom contributions >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

bloomThreshold.description:
minimum brightness the bloom starts having effect
-1:all pixels affect bloom equally (physically correct, faster as a threshold pass is omitted), 0:all pixels affect bloom brights more, 1(default), >1 brighter

bloom1Size.description:
Diameter size for the Bloom1 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/2 resolution, larger values cost more performance, good for high frequency details)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

bloom2Size.description:
Diameter size for Bloom2 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/4 resolution, larger values cost more performance)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

bloom3Size.description:
Diameter size for Bloom3 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/8 resolution, larger values cost more performance)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

bloom4Size.description:
Diameter size for Bloom4 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/16 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

bloom5Size.description:
Diameter size for Bloom5 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/32 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

bloom6Size.description:
Diameter size for Bloom6 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/64 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

bloomConvolutionIntensity.description: Multiplier for Convolution bloom contributions >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

bloomConvolutionScatterDispersion.description: Intensity multiplier on the scatter dispersion energy of the kernel. 1.0 means exactly use the same energy as the kernel scatter dispersion.

bloomConvolutionSize.description: Relative size of the convolution kernel image compared to the minor axis of the viewport

bloomConvolutionTexture.title: /Script/Engine.Texture2D
bloomConvolutionTexture.description: Texture to replace default convolution bloom kernel

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

bloomConvolutionCenterUV.title: Vector2D
bloomConvolutionCenterUV.description: The UV location of the center of the kernel.  Should be very close to (.5,.5)

bloomConvolutionPreFilterMin.description: Boost intensity of select pixels  prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier).  Max < Min disables

bloomConvolutionPreFilterMax.description: Boost intensity of select pixels  prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier).  Max < Min disables

bloomConvolutionPreFilterMult.description: Boost intensity of select pixels  prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier).  Max < Min disables

bloomConvolutionBufferScale.description: Implicit buffer region as a fraction of the screen size to insure the bloom does not wrap across the screen.  Larger sizes have perf impact.

bloomDirtMask.title: /Script/Engine.Texture
bloomDirtMask.description: Texture that defines the dirt on the camera lens where the light of very bright objects is scattered.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

dynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod.title: EDynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod
dynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod.description: Chooses the Dynamic Global Illumination method.  Not compatible with Forward Shading.

indirectLightingColor.title: LinearColor
indirectLightingColor.description: Adjusts indirect lighting color. (1,1,1) is default. (0,0,0) to disable GI. The show flag 'Global Illumination' must be enabled to use this property.

indirectLightingIntensity.description: Scales the indirect lighting contribution. A value of 0 disables GI. Default is 1. The show flag 'Global Illumination' must be enabled to use this property.

lumenRayLightingMode.title: ELumenRayLightingModeOverride
lumenRayLightingMode.description: Controls how Lumen rays are lit when Lumen is using Hardware Ray Tracing.  By default, Lumen uses the Surface Cache for best performance, but can be set to 'Hit Lighting' for higher quality.

lumenSceneLightingQuality.description: Scales Lumen Scene's quality.  Larger scales cause Lumen Scene to be calculated with a higher fidelity, which can be visible in reflections, but increase GPU cost.

lumenSceneDetail.description: Controls the size of instances that can be represented in Lumen Scene.  Larger values will ensure small objects are represented, but increase GPU cost.

lumenSceneViewDistance.description: Sets the maximum view distance of the scene that Lumen maintains for ray tracing against.  Larger values will increase the effective range of sky shadowing and Global Illumination, but increase GPU cost.

lumenSceneLightingUpdateSpeed.description: Controls how much Lumen Scene is allowed to cache lighting results to improve performance.  Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost.

lumenFinalGatherQuality.description: Scales Lumen's Final Gather quality.  Larger scales reduce noise, but greatly increase GPU cost.

lumenFinalGatherLightingUpdateSpeed.description: Controls how much Lumen Final Gather is allowed to cache lighting results to improve performance.  Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost and noise.

lumenFinalGatherScreenTraces.description: Whether to use screen space traces for Lumen Global Illumination. Screen space traces bypass Lumen Scene and instead sample Scene Depth and Scene Color. This improves quality, as it bypasses Lumen Scene, but causes view dependent lighting.

lumenMaxTraceDistance.description: Controls the maximum distance that Lumen should trace while solving lighting.  Values that are too small will cause lighting to leak into large caves, while values that are large will increase GPU cost.

lumenDiffuseColorBoost.description: Allows brightening indirect lighting by calculating material diffuse color for indirect lighting. Values above 1 (original diffuse color) aren't physically correct, but they can be useful as an art direction knob to increase the amount of bounced light in the scene. Best to keep below 2 as it also causes reflections to be brighter than the scene.

lumenAmbientOcclusionIntensity.description: Allows control over the strength of Lumen's Short Range Ambient Occlusion.

lumenSkylightLeaking.description: Controls what fraction of the skylight intensity should be allowed to leak.  This can be useful as an art direction knob (non-physically based) to keep indoor areas from going fully black.

lumenSkylightLeakingTint.title: LinearColor
lumenSkylightLeakingTint.description: Color tint for Lumen Skylight Leaking.

lumenFullSkylightLeakingDistance.description: Controls the distance from a receiving surface where skylight leaking reaches its full intensity.  Smaller values make the skylight leaking flatter, while larger values create an Ambient Occlusion effect.

lumenSurfaceCacheResolution.description: Scale factor for Lumen Surface Cache resolution.  Smaller values save GPU memory, at a cost in quality.  Defaults to 0.5 for Scene Captures if not overridden.

reflectionMethod.title: EReflectionMethod
reflectionMethod.description: Chooses the Reflection method. Not compatible with Forward Shading.

lumenReflectionQuality.description: Scales the Reflection quality.  Larger scales reduce noise in reflections, but increase GPU cost.

lumenReflectionsScreenTraces.description: Whether to use screen space traces for Lumen Reflections. Screen space traces bypass Lumen Scene and instead sample Scene Depth and Scene Color. This improves quality, as it bypasses Lumen Scene, but causes view dependent lighting.

lumenFrontLayerTranslucencyReflections.description: Whether to use high quality mirror reflections on the front layer of translucent surfaces.  Other layers will use the lower quality Radiance Cache method that can only produce glossy reflections.  Increases GPU cost when enabled.

lumenMaxRoughnessToTraceReflections.description: Sets the maximum roughness value for which Lumen still traces dedicated reflection rays. Higher values improve reflection quality, but greatly increase GPU cost.

lumenMaxReflectionBounces.description: Sets the maximum number of recursive reflection bounces. 1 means a single reflection ray (no secondary reflections in mirrors). Currently only supported by Hardware Ray Tracing with Hit Lighting.

lumenMaxRefractionBounces.description: The maximum count of refraction event to trace. When hit lighting is used, Translucent meshes will be traced when LumenMaxRefractionBounces > 0, making the reflection tracing more expenssive.

screenSpaceReflectionIntensity.description: Enable/Fade/disable the Screen Space Reflection feature, in percent, avoid numbers between 0 and 1 fo consistency

screenSpaceReflectionQuality.description: 0=lowest quality..100=maximum quality, only a few quality levels are implemented, no soft transition, 50 is the default for better performance.

screenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness.description: Until what roughness we fade the screen space reflections, 0.8 works well, smaller can run faster

bMegaLights.description:
Allows forcing MegaLights on or off for this volume, regardless of the project setting for MegaLights.
MegaLights will stochastically sample lights, which allows many shadow casting lights to be rendered efficiently, with a consistent and low GPU cost.
When MegaLights is enabled, other direct lighting algorithms like Deferred Shading will no longer be used, and other shadowing methods like Ray Traced Shadows, Distance Field Shadows and Shadow Maps will no longer be used.
MegaLights requires Hardware Ray Tracing and Shader Model 6.

megaLightsFrontLayerTranslucency.description: Whether to use high quality direct lighting on the front layer of translucent surfaces.  Other layers will use the lower quality Translucency Lighting Volume.  Increases GPU cost when enabled.

ambientCubemapIntensity.description:
To scale the Ambient cubemap brightness
>=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

ambientCubemap.title: /Script/Engine.TextureCube
ambientCubemap.description: The Ambient cubemap (Affects diffuse and specular shading), blends additively which if different from all other settings here

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

depthOfFieldFstop.description: Defines the opening of the camera lens, Aperture is 1/fstop, typical lens go down to f/1.2 (large opening), larger numbers reduce the DOF effect

depthOfFieldMinFstop.description: Defines the maximum opening of the camera lens to control the curvature of blades of the diaphragm. Set it to 0 to get straight blades.

depthOfFieldBladeCount.description: Defines the number of blades of the diaphragm within the lens (between 4 and 16).

autoExposureBias.description:
Logarithmic adjustment for the exposure. Only used if a tonemapper is specified.
0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

autoExposureBiasCurve.title: /Script/Engine.CurveFloat
autoExposureBiasCurve.description:
Exposure compensation based on the scene EV100.
Used to calibrate the final exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.
0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

autoExposureMeterMask.title: /Script/Engine.Texture
autoExposureMeterMask.description:
Exposure metering mask. Bright spots on the mask will have high influence on auto-exposure metering
and dark spots will have low influence.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

autoExposureLowPercent.description:
The eye adaptation will adapt to a value extracted from the luminance histogram of the scene color.
The value is defined as having x percent below this brightness. Higher values give bright spots on the screen more priority
but can lead to less stable results. Lower values give the medium and darker values more priority but might cause burn out of
bright spots.
>0, <100, good values are in the range 70 .. 80

autoExposureHighPercent.description:
The eye adaptation will adapt to a value extracted from the luminance histogram of the scene color.
The value is defined as having x percent below this brightness. Higher values give bright spots on the screen more priority
but can lead to less stable results. Lower values give the medium and darker values more priority but might cause burn out of
bright spots.
>0, <100, good values are in the range 80 .. 95

autoExposureMinBrightness.description:
Auto-Exposure minimum adaptation. Eye Adaptation is disabled if Min = Max.
Auto-exposure is implemented by choosing an exposure value for which the average luminance generates a pixel brightness equal to the Constant Calibration value.
The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

autoExposureMaxBrightness.description:
Auto-Exposure maximum adaptation. Eye Adaptation is disabled if Min = Max.
Auto-exposure is implemented by choosing an exposure value for which the average luminance generates a pixel brightness equal to the Constant Calibration value.
The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

autoExposureSpeedUp.description: In F-stops per second, should be >0

autoExposureSpeedDown.description: In F-stops per second, should be >0

histogramLogMin.description: Histogram Min value. Expressed in Log2(Luminance) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings)

histogramLogMax.description: Histogram Max value. Expressed in Log2(Luminance) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings)

localExposureHighlightContrastScale.description:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Contrast of the base layer is reduced based on this value.
Value less than 1 will enable local exposure.
Good values are usually in the range 0.6 .. 1.0.

localExposureShadowContrastScale.description:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Contrast of the base layer is reduced based on this value.
Value less than 1 will enable local exposure.
Good values are usually in the range 0.6 .. 1.0.

localExposureHighlightContrastCurve.title: /Script/Engine.CurveFloat
localExposureHighlightContrastCurve.description:
Local Exposure Highlight Contrast based on the scene EV100.
Used to calibrate Local Exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

localExposureShadowContrastCurve.title: /Script/Engine.CurveFloat
localExposureShadowContrastCurve.description:
Local Exposure Shadow Contrast based on the scene EV100.
Used to calibrate Local Exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

localExposureHighlightThreshold.description: Threshold used to determine which regions of the screen are considered highlights.

localExposureShadowThreshold.description: Threshold used to determine which regions of the screen are considered shadows.

localExposureDetailStrength.description:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Value different than 1 will enable local exposure.
This value should be set to 1 in most cases.

localExposureBlurredLuminanceBlend.description:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Blend between bilateral filtered and blurred luminance as the base layer.
Blurred luminance helps preserve image appearance and specular highlights, and reduce ringing.
Good values are usually in the range 0.4 .. 0.6

localExposureBlurredLuminanceKernelSizeP.description: Kernel size (percentage of screen) used to blur frame luminance.

localExposureMiddleGreyBias.description:
Logarithmic adjustment for the local exposure middle grey.
0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

lensFlareIntensity.description: Brightness scale of the image cased lens flares (linear)

lensFlareTint.title: LinearColor
lensFlareTint.description: Tint color for the image based lens flares.

lensFlareBokehSize.description: Size of the Lens Blur (in percent of the view width) that is done with the Bokeh texture (note: performance cost is radius*radius)

lensFlareThreshold.description: Minimum brightness the lens flare starts having effect (this should be as high as possible to avoid the performance cost of blurring content that is too dark too see)

lensFlareBokehShape.title: /Script/Engine.Texture
lensFlareBokehShape.description: Defines the shape of the Bokeh when the image base lens flares are blurred, cannot be blended

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

lensFlareTints.description: RGB defines the lens flare color, A it's position. This is a temporary solution.

vignetteType.title: EVignetteType
vignetteType.description: The shape type of the vignette

vignetteCenter.title: Vector2f
vignetteCenter.description: Position of the vignette center in UV space.

vignetteColor.title: LinearColor
vignetteColor.description: Color multiplied with areas that are masked by the vignette. Default is black.

vignetteSize.title: Vector2f
vignetteSize.description: Scale of the vignette shape in screenspace. Can be used to scale vignette anamorphically. Default is 1.

vignetteSoftness.description: The softness of the transition from opaque to transparant on the edge of the vignette shape.

vignetteTexture.title: /Script/Engine.Texture
vignetteTexture.description: Defines the shape of the vignette when VignetteType is set to Texture

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

sharpen.description: Controls the strength of image sharpening applied during tonemapping.

filmGrainIntensity.description: 0..1 Film grain intensity to apply. LinearSceneColor *= lerp(1.0, DecodedFilmGrainTexture, FilmGrainIntensity)

filmGrainIntensityShadows.description: Control over the grain intensity in the regions of the image considered shadow areas.

filmGrainIntensityMidtones.description: Control over the grain intensity in the mid-tone region of the image.

filmGrainIntensityHighlights.description: Control over the grain intensity in the regions of the image considered highlight areas.

filmGrainShadowsMax.description: Sets the upper bound used for Film Grain Shadow Intensity.

filmGrainHighlightsMin.description: Sets the lower bound used for Film Grain Highlight Intensity.

filmGrainHighlightsMax.description: Sets the upper bound used for Film Grain Highlight Intensity. This value should be larger than HighlightsMin.. Default is 1.0, for backwards compatibility

filmGrainScale.title: Vector2f
filmGrainScale.description: Controls the size of the film grain. Size of texel of FilmGrainTexture on screen.

filmGrainTexture.title: /Script/Engine.Texture2D
filmGrainTexture.description: Defines film grain texture to use.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

ambientOcclusionIntensity.description: 0..1 0=off/no ambient occlusion .. 1=strong ambient occlusion, defines how much it affects the non direct lighting after base pass

ambientOcclusionStaticFraction.description: 0..1 0=no effect on static lighting .. 1=AO affects the stat lighting, 0 is free meaning no extra rendering pass

ambientOcclusionRadius.description: >0, in unreal units, bigger values means even distant surfaces affect the ambient occlusion

ambientOcclusionRadiusInWS.description: true: AO radius is in world space units, false: AO radius is locked the view space in 400 units

ambientOcclusionFadeDistance.description: >0, in unreal units, at what distance the AO effect disppears in the distance (avoding artifacts and AO effects on huge object)

ambientOcclusionFadeRadius.description: >0, in unreal units, how many units before AmbientOcclusionFadeOutDistance it starts fading out

ambientOcclusionPower.description: >0, in unreal units, bigger values means even distant surfaces affect the ambient occlusion

ambientOcclusionBias.description: >0, in unreal units, default (3.0) works well for flat surfaces but can reduce details

ambientOcclusionQuality.description: 0=lowest quality..100=maximum quality, only a few quality levels are implemented, no soft transition

ambientOcclusionMipBlend.description: Affects the blend over the multiple mips (lower resolution versions) , 0:fully use full resolution, 1::fully use low resolution, around 0.6 seems to be a good value

ambientOcclusionMipScale.description: Affects the radius AO radius scale over the multiple mips (lower resolution versions)

ambientOcclusionMipThreshold.description: to tweak the bilateral upsampling when using multiple mips (lower resolution versions)

ambientOcclusionTemporalBlendWeight.description: How much to blend the current frame with previous frames when using GTAO with temporal accumulation

rayTracingAOSamplesPerPixel.description: Sets the samples per pixel for ray tracing ambient occlusion.

rayTracingAOIntensity.description: Scalar factor on the ray-tracing ambient occlusion score.

rayTracingAORadius.description: Defines the world-space search radius for occlusion rays.

colorGradingIntensity.description: Color grading lookup table intensity. 0 = no intensity, 1=full intensity

colorGradingLUT.title: /Script/Engine.Texture
colorGradingLUT.description: Look up table texture to use or none of not used

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

depthOfFieldEnabled.description: When false, post-process depth of field will not be used. When true, DoF may be used depending on lens and scalability settings.

depthOfFieldSensorWidth.description: Width of the camera sensor to assume, in mm.

depthOfFieldSqueezeFactor.description: This is the squeeze factor for the DOF, which emulates the properties of anamorphic lenses.

depthOfFieldFocalDistance.description: Distance in which the Depth of Field effect should be sharp, in unreal units (cm)

depthOfFieldDepthBlurAmount.description: CircleDOF only: Depth blur km for 50%

depthOfFieldDepthBlurRadius.description: CircleDOF only: Depth blur radius in pixels at 1920x

depthOfFieldUseHairDepth.description: For depth of field to use the hair depth for computing circle of confusion size. Otherwise use an interpolated distance between the hair depth and the scene depth based on the hair coverage (default).

depthOfFieldPetzvalBokeh.description: Simulate stretching in blur and bokeh. Positive values for sagittal (swirly bokeh), negative values for tangential.

depthOfFieldPetzvalBokehFalloff.description: How quickly does the Petzval bokeh effect increase towards the edge of the image

depthOfFieldPetzvalExclusionBoxExtents.title: Vector2f
depthOfFieldPetzvalExclusionBoxExtents.description: Box, centered on screen, around which the Petzval effect is applied.

depthOfFieldAspectRatioScalar.description: Amount to scale the output viewport's aspect ratio by when computing depth of field properties.

depthOfFieldBarrelRadius.description: The lens barrel creates vignetting and occludes bokeh, i.e. cat's eye bokeh

depthOfFieldBarrelLength.description: The lens barrel creates vignetting and occludes bokeh, i.e. cat's eye bokeh

pitch.description: Angle of the panel with the lens barrel

roll.description: Rotation of the panel around the lens barrel

depthOfFieldMatteBoxFlags.description: Panels around the front of the lens barrel that occlude bokeh

depthOfFieldFocalRegion.description: Artificial region where all content is in focus, starting after DepthOfFieldFocalDistance, in unreal units  (cm)

depthOfFieldNearTransitionRegion.description: To define the width of the transition region next to the focal region on the near side (cm)

depthOfFieldFarTransitionRegion.description: To define the width of the transition region next to the focal region on the near side (cm)

depthOfFieldScale.description:
SM5: BokehDOF only: To amplify the depth of field effect (like aperture)  0=off
          ES3_1: Used to blend DoF. 0=off

depthOfFieldNearBlurSize.description: Gaussian only: Maximum size of the Depth of Field blur (in percent of the view width) (note: performance cost scales with size)

depthOfFieldFarBlurSize.description: Gaussian only: Maximum size of the Depth of Field blur (in percent of the view width) (note: performance cost scales with size)

depthOfFieldOcclusion.description: Occlusion tweak factor 1 (0.18 to get natural occlusion, 0.4 to solve layer color leaking issues)

depthOfFieldSkyFocusDistance.description: Artificial distance to allow the skybox to be in focus (e.g. 200000), <=0 to switch the feature off, only for GaussianDOF, can cost performance

depthOfFieldVignetteSize.description: Artificial circular mask to (near) blur content outside the radius, only for GaussianDOF, diameter in percent of screen width, costs performance if the mask is used, keep Feather can Radius on default to keep it off

motionBlurMax.description: max distortion caused by motion blur, in percent of the screen width, 0:off

motionBlurTargetFPS.description:
Defines the target FPS for motion blur. Makes motion blur independent of actual frame rate and relative
to the specified target FPS instead. Higher target FPS results in shorter frames, which means shorter
shutter times and less motion blur. Lower FPS means more motion blur. A value of zero makes the motion
blur dependent on the actual frame rate.

motionBlurPerObjectSize.description: The minimum projected screen radius for a primitive to be drawn in the velocity pass, percentage of screen width. smaller numbers cause more draw calls, default: 4%

rayTracingTranslucencyMaxRoughness.description: Sets the maximum roughness until which ray tracing translucency will be visible (lower value is faster). Translucency contribution is smoothly faded when close to roughness threshold. This parameter behaves similarly to ScreenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness.

rayTracingTranslucencyRefractionRays.description: Sets the maximum number of ray tracing refraction rays.

rayTracingTranslucencySamplesPerPixel.description: Sets the samples per pixel for ray traced translucency.

rayTracingTranslucencyMaxPrimaryHitEvent.description: Maximum number of hit events allowed on primary ray paths

rayTracingTranslucencyMaxSecondaryHitEve.description: Maximum number of hit events allowed on secondary ray paths

rayTracingTranslucencyRefraction.description: Sets whether refraction should be enabled or not (if not rays will not scatter and only travel in the same direction as before the intersection event).

rayTracingTranslucencyUseRayTracedRefrac.description: Whether to use ray traced refraction which currently doesn't work well with rough refraction or simulate it using a screen space effect

pathTracingMaxBounces.description: Sets the path tracing maximum bounces

pathTracingSamplesPerPixel.description: Sets the samples per pixel for the path tracer.

pathTracingMaxPathIntensity.description: Sets the maximum intensity of indirect samples to reduce fireflies. Lowering this value reduces noise at the expense of accuracy. Increasing it is more accurate but may lead to more noise.

pathTracingEnableEmissiveMaterials.description: Should emissive materials contribute to scene lighting?

pathTracingEnableReferenceDOF.description: Enables a reference quality depth-of-field which replaces the post-process effect.

pathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere.description: Enables path tracing in the atmosphere instead of baking the sky atmosphere contribution into a skylight. Any skylight present in the scene will be automatically ignored when this is enabled.

pathTracingEnableDenoiser.description: Run the currently loaded denoiser plugin on the last sample to remove noise from the output. Has no effect if a plug-in is not loaded.

pathTracingIncludeEmissive.description: Should the render include directly visible emissive elements?

pathTracingIncludeDiffuse.description: Should the render include diffuse lighting contributions?

pathTracingIncludeIndirectDiffuse.description: Should the render include indirect diffuse lighting contributions?

pathTracingIncludeSpecular.description: Should the render include specular lighting contributions?

pathTracingIncludeIndirectSpecular.description: Should the render include indirect specular lighting contributions?

pathTracingIncludeVolume.description: Should the render include volume lighting contributions?

pathTracingIncludeIndirectVolume.description: Should the render include volume lighting contributions?

userFlags.description: Per-view user flags accessible in materials via TestPostVolumeUserFlag node, allowing per-view overrides of material behavior.

weightedBlendables.title: WeightedBlendables
weightedBlendables.description:
Allows custom post process materials to be defined, using a MaterialInstance with the same Material as its parent to allow blending.
For materials this needs to be the "PostProcess" domain type. This can be used for any UObject object implementing the IBlendableInterface (e.g. could be used to fade weather settings).

object.title: /Script/CoreUObject.Object
object.description: should be of the IBlendableInterface* type but UProperties cannot express that

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

priority.description:
Priority of this volume. In the case of overlapping volumes the one with the highest priority
overrides the lower priority ones. The order is undefined if two or more overlapping volumes have the same priority.

blendRadius.description: World space radius around the volume that is used for blending (only if not unbound).

bEnabled.description: Whether this volume is enabled or not.

bUnbound.description: Whether this volume covers the whole world, or just the area inside its bounds.

brushComponent.title: /Script/Engine.BrushComponent
brushComponent.description: Represents a reference to a UObject or UClass.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

brushBuilder.title: /Script/Engine.BrushBuilder
brushBuilder.description: Represents a reference to a UObject or UClass.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

bDisplayShadedVolume.description: If true, display the brush with a shaded volume

shadedVolumeOpacityValue.description: Value used to set the opacity for the shaded volume, between 0-1

primaryActorTick.title: ActorTickFunction

tickGroup.title: ETickingGroup
tickGroup.description:
Defines the first tick group where this function can be executed.
These groups determine the relative order of when objects tick during a frame update.
If this function has prerequisites, execution may be delayed to a later group.

endTickGroup.title: ETickingGroup
endTickGroup.description:
Defines the tick group that this tick function must finish within.
Normal synchronous ticks do not need to set this manually.
The game thread will stall at the end of this group if the function (or a spawned task) is still in progress.

bTickEvenWhenPaused.description: Bool indicating that this function should execute even if the gameplay is paused. Pause ticks are very limited in capabilities.

bStartWithTickEnabled.description: If true, this tick function will start enabled, but can be disabled later on.

bAllowTickOnDedicatedServer.description: If we allow this tick to run on a dedicated server

tickInterval.description: The time in seconds between executions of this tick function. If <= 0 then it will tick every frame.

bOnlyRelevantToOwner.description: If true, this actor is only relevant to its owner. If this flag is changed during play, all non-owner channels would need to be explicitly closed.

bHidden.description:
Allows us to only see this Actor in the Editor, and not in the actual game.
@see SetActorHiddenInGame()

bIsMainWorldOnly.description: If checked, this Actor will only get loaded in a main world (persistent level), it will not be loaded through Level Instances.

bNetLoadOnClient.description: This actor will be loaded on network clients during map load

bNetUseOwnerRelevancy.description: If actor has valid Owner, call Owner's IsNetRelevantFor and GetNetPriority

bRelevantForLevelBounds.description:
If true, this actor's component's bounds will be included in the level's
bounding box unless the Actor's class has overridden IsLevelBoundsRelevant

bReplayRewindable.description:
If true, this actor will only be destroyed during scrubbing if the replay is set to a time before the actor existed.
Otherwise, RewindForReplay will be called if we detect the actor needs to be reset.
Note, this Actor must not be destroyed by gamecode, and RollbackViaDeletion may not be used.

bAllowTickBeforeBeginPlay.description:
Whether we allow this Actor to tick before it receives the BeginPlay event.
Normally we don't tick actors until after BeginPlay; this setting allows this behavior to be overridden.
This Actor must be able to tick for this setting to be relevant.

bAutoDestroyWhenFinished.description: If true then destroy self when "finished", meaning all relevant components report that they are done and no timelines or timers are in flight.

bBlockInput.description: If true, all input on the stack below this actor will not be considered

bFindCameraComponentWhenViewTarget.description: If true, this actor should search for an owned camera component to view through when used as a view target.

bIgnoresOriginShifting.description: Whether this actor should not be affected by world origin shifting.

bEnableAutoLODGeneration.description: Whether this actor should be considered or not during HLOD generation.

bIsEditorOnlyActor.description: Whether this actor is editor-only. Use with care, as if this actor is referenced by anything else that reference will be NULL in cooked builds

bReplicates.description:
If true, this actor will replicate to remote machines
@see SetReplicates()

bCanBeInCluster.description: If true, this actor can be put inside of a GC Cluster to improve Garbage Collection performance

bMigratingAsset.description: If true, this actor can be migrated to another server even if it's been loaded from disk

bReplicateUsingRegisteredSubObjectList.description:
When true the replication system will only replicate the registered subobjects and the replicated actor components list
When false the replication system will instead call the virtual ReplicateSubobjects() function where the subobjects and actor components need to be manually replicated.

bAsyncPhysicsTickEnabled.description: Whether to use use the async physics tick with this actor.

updateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelStreaming.title: EActorUpdateOverlapsMethod
updateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelStreaming.description:
Condition for calling UpdateOverlaps() to initialize overlap state when loaded in during level streaming.
If set to 'UseConfigDefault', the default specified in ini (displayed in 'DefaultUpdateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelStreaming') will be used.
If overlaps are not initialized, this actor and attached components will not have an initial state of what objects are touching it,
and overlap events may only come in once one of those objects update overlaps themselves (for example when moving).
However if an object touching it *does* initialize state, both objects will know about their touching state with each other.
This can be a potentially large performance savings during level loading and streaming, and is safe if the object and others initially
overlapping it do not need the overlap state because they will not trigger overlap notifications.

Note that if 'bGenerateOverlapEventsDuringLevelStreaming' is true, overlaps are always updated in this case, but that flag
determines whether the Begin/End overlap events are triggered.

@see bGenerateOverlapEventsDuringLevelStreaming, DefaultUpdateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelStreaming, GetUpdateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelStreaming()

defaultUpdateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelSt.title: EActorUpdateOverlapsMethod
defaultUpdateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelSt.description:
Default value taken from config file for this class when 'UseConfigDefault' is chosen for
'UpdateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelStreaming'. This allows a default to be chosen per class in the matching config.
For example, for Actor it could be specified in DefaultEngine.ini as:

[/Script/Engine.Actor]
DefaultUpdateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelStreaming = OnlyUpdateMovable

Another subclass could set their default to something different, such as:

[/Script/Engine.BlockingVolume]
DefaultUpdateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelStreaming = NeverUpdate

@see UpdateOverlapsMethodDuringLevelStreaming

remoteRole.title: ENetRole
remoteRole.description: Describes how much control the remote machine has over the actor.

initialLifeSpan.description: How long this Actor lives before dying, 0=forever. Note this is the INITIAL value and should not be modified once play has begun.

customTimeDilation.description: Allow each actor to run at a different time speed. The DeltaTime for a frame is multiplied by the global TimeDilation (in WorldSettings) and this CustomTimeDilation for this actor's tick.

runtimeGrid.description:
Determine in which partition grid this actor will be placed in the partition (if the world is partitioned).
If None, the decision will be left to the partition.

replicatedMovement.title: RepMovement
replicatedMovement.description: Used for replication of our RootComponent's position and velocity

locationQuantizationLevel.title: EVectorQuantization
locationQuantizationLevel.description: Allows tuning the compression level for the replicated location vector. You should only need to change this from the default if you see visual artifacts.

velocityQuantizationLevel.title: EVectorQuantization
velocityQuantizationLevel.description: Allows tuning the compression level for the replicated velocity vectors. You should only need to change this from the default if you see visual artifacts.

rotationQuantizationLevel.title: ERotatorQuantization
rotationQuantizationLevel.description: Allows tuning the compression level for replicated rotation. You should only need to change this from the default if you see visual artifacts.

role.title: ENetRole
role.description: Describes how much control the local machine has over the actor.

netDormancy.title: ENetDormancy
netDormancy.description: Dormancy setting for actor to take itself off of the replication list without being destroyed on clients.

spawnCollisionHandlingMethod.title: ESpawnActorCollisionHandlingMethod
spawnCollisionHandlingMethod.description: Controls how to handle spawning this actor in a situation where it's colliding with something else. "Default" means AlwaysSpawn here.

autoReceiveInput.title: EAutoReceiveInput
autoReceiveInput.description: Automatically registers this actor to receive input from a player.

inputPriority.description: The priority of this input component when pushed in to the stack.

netPriority.description: Priority for this actor when checking for replication in a low bandwidth or saturated situation, higher priority means it is more likely to replicate

physicsReplicationMode.title: EPhysicsReplicationMode
physicsReplicationMode.description: Which mode to replicate physics through for this actor. Only relevant if the actor replicates movement and has a component that simulate physics.

instigator.title: /Script/Engine.Pawn
instigator.description: Pawn responsible for damage and other gameplay events caused by this actor.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

rootComponent.title: /Script/Engine.SceneComponent
rootComponent.description: The component that defines the transform (location, rotation, scale) of this Actor in the world, all other components must be attached to this one somehow

pivotOffset.title: Vector
pivotOffset.description: Local space pivot offset for the actor, only used in the editor

hLODLayer.title: /Script/Engine.HLODLayer
hLODLayer.description: The UHLODLayer in which this actor should be included.

layers.description: Layers the actor belongs to.  This is outside of the editoronly data to allow hiding of LD-specified layers at runtime for profiling.

contentBundleGuid.description: The GUID for this actor's content bundle.

refPath.description: The reference stored as a soft path string.

externalDataLayerAsset.description: Represents a reference to a UObject or UClass.

spriteScale.description: The scale to apply to any billboard components in editor builds (happens in any WITH_EDITOR build, including non-cooked games).

bOptimizeBPComponentData.description: Whether to cook additional data to speed up spawn events at runtime for any Blueprint classes based on this Actor. This option may slightly increase memory usage in a cooked build.

bIsSpatiallyLoaded.description:
Determine if this actor is spatially loaded when placed in a partitioned world.
     If true, this actor will be loaded when in the range of any streaming sources and if (1) in no data layers, or (2) one or more of its data layers are enabled.
     If false, this actor will be loaded if (1) in no data layers, or (2) one or more of its data layers are enabled.

tags.description: Array of tags that can be used for grouping and categorizing.
